title: The heart
note: A frontal section seen from the front: the patient's right is on your left, so the right atrium and right ventricle (blue, deoxygenated blood) sit on the left of the image. Red vessels carry oxygenated blood.

src.t: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy

items.ex: Receives deoxygenated blood from the superior and inferior venae cavae.
Pumps deoxygenated blood through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk.
Receives oxygenated blood from the pulmonary veins.
Has the thickest wall and pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta for the systemic circuit.
Carries oxygenated blood from the left ventricle to the systemic circuit.
Carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle and divides into the pulmonary arteries.
Returns blood from regions above the diaphragm to the right atrium.
Returns blood from regions below the diaphragm to the right atrium.
Carry oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium.
Three-cusped right atrioventricular valve between the right atrium and right ventricle.
Two-cusped (bicuspid) left atrioventricular valve between the left atrium and left ventricle.
Semilunar valve at the base of the aorta that prevents backflow into the left ventricle.
Semilunar valve at the base of the pulmonary trunk that prevents backflow into the right ventricle.
Thick muscular wall that separates the right and left ventricles.

title: The neuron
note: A multipolar motor neuron: many dendrites and a single axon. Signals run left to right, from the dendrites and cell body down the myelinated axon to the terminals.

src.t: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 12.2 Nervous Tissue

items.ex: Branched processes that receive signals from other neurons at synapses.
Contains the nucleus and most of the neuron's major organelles.
Holds the cell's DNA inside the cell body.
Tapering cone where the axon leaves the cell body; it leads into the trigger zone where action potentials start.
Single long fiber that carries the nerve impulse away from the cell body to target cells.
Glial wrapping (Schwann cells in this peripheral neuron) that insulates the axon and speeds conduction.
Gap in the myelin where the action potential is regenerated as it jumps down the axon.
Branched axon endings whose synaptic end bulbs release neurotransmitter onto the target cell.

title: The brain
note: The left hemisphere seen from the side, with the front of the head on your left. The central sulcus divides frontal from parietal lobe, and the lateral sulcus sets off the temporal lobe.

src.t: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 13.2 The Central Nervous System

items.ex: Lies anterior to the central sulcus; holds the primary motor cortex and Broca's area.
Lies posterior to the central sulcus; its postcentral gyrus is the primary somatosensory cortex.
Lies below the lateral sulcus; contains the primary auditory cortex and helps form long-term memories.
Forms the posterior cerebrum and contains the primary visual cortex.
Compares motor commands with sensory feedback to coordinate movement.
Midbrain, pons and medulla; links the cerebrum to the spinal cord and regulates vital functions.
Groove separating the frontal lobe in front from the parietal lobe behind.
Deep groove separating the temporal lobe from the frontal and parietal lobes.

title: The nephron
note: One nephron and its blood supply. Blood is filtered at the renal corpuscle (top left); the filtrate then flows through the tubule, down and back up the loop of Henle, to the collecting duct on the right.

src.t: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 25.4 Microscopic Anatomy of the Kidney

items.ex: Tuft of fenestrated capillaries between the afferent and efferent arterioles where blood is filtered.
Double-walled cup whose podocyte layer wraps the glomerulus; it collects the filtrate.

d: Descending limb of the loop of Henle
items.ex: Main site of reabsorption; its brush border and many mitochondria drive uptake of Na+, Cl- and glucose.

items.a: Descending limb of the loop of Henle
d: Ascending limb of the loop of Henle
items.ex: Has permanent aquaporins, so water leaves the filtrate as it descends into the medulla.

items.a: Ascending limb of the loop of Henle
d: Descending limb of the loop of Henle
items.ex: Lacks aquaporins, so it is impermeable to water while Na+ and Cl- leave the filtrate.

d: Ascending limb of the loop of Henle
items.ex: Shorter than the PCT; its first part forms the macula densa beside the afferent arteriole.

d: Ascending limb of the loop of Henle
items.ex: Drains several nephrons; ADH inserts aquaporins here so more water is recovered.
Wider arteriole that brings blood into the glomerulus; its juxtaglomerular cells adjust that flow.
Narrower arteriole that carries blood out of the glomerulus; constricting it sustains filtration pressure.

title: The eye
note: The eye cut through its center, with the cornea facing left and the optic nerve leaving the back on the right. The wall has three layers, from outside in: sclera, choroid, retina.

src.t: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 14.1 Sensory Perception

items.ex: Transparent front of the outer fibrous layer; it admits light and helps focus it.
Colored smooth muscle ring that narrows the pupil in bright light and widens it in dim light.
Central opening in the iris that lets light into the eye.
Works with the cornea to focus light; the ciliary body changes its shape.
Muscular ring attached to the lens by suspensory ligaments; it bends the lens to focus.
Tough white outer layer covering about five sixths of the eye's surface.
Highly vascular layer that supplies blood to the eyeball.
Innermost neural layer where rods and cones turn light into neural signals.
Small central pit of the retina with only photoreceptors; the point of sharpest vision.
Retinal ganglion cell axons leaving at the optic disc, which creates the blind spot.
Thick, gel-like fluid filling the posterior cavity behind the lens.
Space between the cornea and iris filled with watery aqueous humor.

title: The respiratory tract
note: The upper airway is drawn in side profile with the face to your left; the chest is an anterior view, so the patient's right lung (three lobes) is on your left, and the inset magnifies alveoli at the end of a bronchiole.

src.t: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 22.1 Organs and Structures of the Respiratory System

items.ex: Air passage whose conchae and mucosa clean, warm and moisten incoming air.
Muscular tube behind the nasal and oral cavities; its lower parts carry both air and food.
Cartilaginous structure joining the pharynx to the trachea; it holds the vocal cords and epiglottis.
Airway held open by 16 to 20 C-shaped rings of hyaline cartilage.
Shorter, wider and more vertical than the left; it enters the right lung at the hilum.
Longer, narrower and more horizontal than the right; it enters the left lung at the hilum.
Small airways about 1 mm across, with smooth muscle but no cartilage, that adjust airflow.
Grape-like sacs whose thin walls form the respiratory membrane for gas exchange.
Dome-shaped muscle at the base of the thoracic cavity; it contracts to draw air in.
Has three lobes (superior, middle, inferior) and is shorter and wider than the left lung.
Has two lobes and a cardiac notch that makes room for the heart.
